title: When polynomials cannot hide the difference
standfirst: A short argument from complex dynamics offers a general answer to Furter's rigidity problem—and changes which calculations are worth doing next.
summary: A popular explanation of the candidate polynomial-composition rigidity proof, its critical-value argument, and what it does and does not settle for seven Evidence Press releases.
claimBoundary: AI-assisted explanation of liqsweep's external unrefereed candidate at source commit b17b6b9. Internal mathematical source review found no load-bearing gap in the central argument; formal verification, unaffiliated specialist review and priority have not been established. Consequences depend on that argument and the cited prior theorems. This article is not a new Evidence Press research result or an independent verification.

banner.alt: An ivory identity line and a gold polynomial curve meet near the centre, then separate against a dark teal grid.
banner.caption: The identity and z − 2z³ + z⁴ on a real slice near zero. Their matching low-order terms conceal a cubic difference. This illustration is not a picture of complex attracting basins.
